initial: Generate a scramble to see the sequence.
noStats: Your session results will appear here.
solverText: The step-by-step solver is planned for phase 4.
rightLesson: Facing the right side, R turns that face 90° clockwise. R′ reverses the turn.
train: Practice this case and solve it with the inverse move.
copyFailed: Select the sequence to copy it.
startInspect: Tap here or press Space to start inspection.
startHold: Press and hold. Release when you see “Ready”.
pendingSave: Attempt pending. Saving will be retried.
notationError: Check position {position}. Separate turns with spaces, for example R U2 F′.
invalidTime: Enter a positive time in seconds or minutes:seconds with up to two decimal places. Examples: 12.34 and 1:02.34.
noTimes: No attempts in this session yet.
confirmArchive: Archive this session? You can restore it later.
confirmMerge: Move all attempts to the destination and archive the source session?
confirmMove: Move selected attempts to the destination session?
invalidBackup: The backup contains invalid or conflicting data. Import was cancelled.
fingerUpper: Try an index flick for U and the opposite index for U′. For U2, combine index and middle flicks.
fingerSlice: For M2, try two successive ring and middle finger flicks. Keep the outer layers together.
aMove_prime: Prime. A counterclockwise quarter turn when facing that face.
aMove_R2: A half turn of the right face.
aMove_x: The whole cube in the R direction.
aMove_y: The whole cube in the U direction.
aMove_z: The whole cube in the F direction.
aMove_M: Middle slice between L and R, in the L direction.
aMove_E: Middle slice between D and U, in the D direction.
aMove_S: Middle slice between F and B, in the F direction.
aBody_notationB: A letter means a clockwise quarter turn viewed from the face. Prime reverses it and 2 means a half turn. x, y, z rotate the whole cube.
aExercise_notationB: From solved, do R and undo it with R′. Check your starting state.
aGoal_cross: Align the four white edges with the side centers.
aBody_cross: Find a white edge, align its other color to the center, and bring it down to D. Check from the side.
aExercise_cross: Find the edge displaced by F2 and restore the cross without rotating the cube.
aQuiz_cross_1: Four white stickers are enough even if the sides do not match.
aQuiz_cross_2: The side center identifies the edge slot.
aGoal_corners: Complete D and preserve the cross.
aBody_corners: Identify a corner by its three colors. Use U to bring it to the front-right slot. If it is in the wrong slot, extract it first and reorient it.
aExercise_corners: Point to the unsolved slot and restore its matching corner.
aQuiz_corners_1: All three colors identify its slot.
aGoal_middle: Insert middle-layer edges without losing D.
aBody_middle: Look in U for an edge without yellow. Match its front color with the center and check whether the other color goes left or right. For the other side, rotate the cube and practise inserting from the new front.
aExercise_middle: Identify the front-right edge in the example and trace where it moves.
aQuiz_middle_0: I look for an edge without yellow.
aQuiz_middle_1: The other color identifies the slot.
aQuiz_middle_2: D must be undone for insertion.
aBody_yellowCross: A line has two opposite yellow edges, the L has two adjacent ones, and a dot has none. Turn U to match the animated case.
aExercise_yellowCross: Set up line, L, and dot. Count only the edge stickers.
aQuiz_yellowCross_0: The line has two opposite edges.
aQuiz_yellowCross_1: The dot has four oriented edges.
aQuiz_yellowCross_2: Corners do not determine the cross shape.
aGoal_orient: Complete the top color after making the cross.
aBody_orient: Sune and Anti-Sune have one oriented corner. Check the direction of the other three side stickers. All seven shapes are in 2-look OLL.
aExercise_orient: Distinguish Sune from Anti-Sune before playing the sequence.
aQuiz_orient_2: Orientation changes which color faces up.
aGoal_permCorners: Order U corners while preserving orientation.
aBody_permCorners: Look for two corner stickers matching on one side. One pair indicates adjacent T, none diagonal Y. With four pairs, only adjust U.
aExercise_permCorners: Set up T and Y and compare which one shows a matching side pair.
aQuiz_permCorners_0: A matching side pair indicates the adjacent case.
aQuiz_permCorners_1: An oriented corner is always in its slot.
aQuiz_permCorners_2: The diagonal case has no matching side pair.
aGoal_permEdges: Finish the last layer after aligning corners.
aBody_permEdges: Ua and Ub cycle three edges in opposite directions. H swaps opposite edges and Z swaps adjacent ones. Adjust U at the end if needed.
aExercise_permEdges: Predict where one edge will finish before animating each case.
aQuiz_permEdges_0: H leaves one U edge fixed.
aQuiz_permEdges_1: Ua and Ub cycle in opposite directions.
aQuiz_permEdges_2: A final U adjustment can align the layer.
aGoal_crossPlan: Plan during inspection with the cross on D.
aBody_crossPlan: Trace all four edges before turning. Try to advance more than one per turn and rehearse the sequence mentally.
aExercise_crossPlan: From F2 R2, predict the order of repairs and perform them without stopping.
aQuiz_crossPlan_1: One move can advance two edges.
aQuiz_crossPlan_2: Every edge requires rotating the whole cube.
aGoal_f2l: Recognize, join, and insert a pair with the cross on D.
aBody_f2l: When a pair is joined, bring it next to the slot and insert. If separated, move one piece out of the way, align the other with U, and join. Split a mismatched pair by temporarily opening the slot.
aExercise_f2l: In each example point to the corner, its edge, and the slot before turning.
aQuiz_f2l_0: A pair uses one corner and one edge.
aQuiz_f2l_2: Close an open slot after insertion.
aGoal_oll3: Recognize three edge shapes and seven corner shapes.
aBody_oll3: Start with dot, L, or line. With an oriented cross, count oriented corners and compare side stickers with the setup. H and Pi have zero, Sune and Anti-Sune one, and T, L, U two.
aExercise_oll3: Open the ten cases and separate edge recognition from corner recognition.
aQuiz_oll3_0: OLL has to permute the last layer.
aGoal_pll3: Order corners then edges with six cases.
aBody_pll3: Separate adjacent and diagonal corner cases. Align the corners before choosing Ua, Ub, H, or Z. Compare adjacent and opposite edges.
aExercise_pll3: Identify the pieces swapped in each setup.
aQuiz_pll3_1: T and Y cover the first recognition step.
aGoal_firstLayer: Build D with matching side pairs.
aBody_firstLayer: Start with a corner and add its neighbors using their shared colors. Check the bottom color and all four side pairs.
aExercise_firstLayer: Restore the front-right corner and check matching pairs.
aQuiz_firstLayer_0: The first layer has matching side pairs.
aQuiz_firstLayer_1: A white face guarantees a layer.
aGoal_orient2: Put the U color on all four corners.
aBody_orient2: Compare the side stickers of Sune and Anti-Sune. For other shapes the Ortega module shows each orientation directly.
aExercise_orient2: Distinguish the two cases with just one oriented corner.
aQuiz_orient2_1: The top face can be complete before permutation.
aQuiz_orient2_2: Orientation puts corners in their slots.
aGoal_perm2: Finish with an adjacent or diagonal swap.
aBody_perm2: With U oriented, one pair indicates adjacent and no pairs indicates diagonal. If all four match, align U with D.
aExercise_perm2: Compare the two setups and identify the matching pair before moving.
aQuiz_perm2_0: Diagonal has a matching side pair.
aQuiz_perm2_1: Adjacent leaves a matching side pair.
aQuiz_perm2_2: The bottom face must be preserved.
aGoal_firstFace: Build D without requiring matching sides.
aBody_firstFace: Pick the easiest color. If the face is formed with mismatched sides, continue to OLL. PBL fixes both layers.
aExercise_firstFace: Restore the face from the setup and distinguish a face from a layer.
aQuiz_firstFace_0: Ortega can start on any color.
aQuiz_firstFace_1: Pairs are required in the first step.
aBody_oll2: Count upward stickers of the top color. One means Sune or Anti-Sune, zero H or Pi, and two T, L, or U. Turn U to match the example.
aExercise_oll2: Classify each case by looking at U and two sides before playing.
aQuiz_oll2_0: H and Pi have no upward corners initially.
aBody_pbl2: In each layer, four pairs means ordered, one means adjacent, and zero means diagonal. If only D needs fixing, flip the cube and use the single-layer case.
aExercise_pbl2: Count the pairs on both layers before choosing a case.
aQuiz_pbl2_0: A diagonal swap has a matching side pair.
aQuiz_pbl2_1: An adjacent swap leaves a matching side pair.
aFrame: Before setting up the case, hold the solved cube with white on the bottom and green in front.
aIdentify: Identify the case shown on the cube.
fingerRight: Try R′ with the right wrist while the left hand holds the cube.
fingerHalf: Turn the face halfway in one smooth motion. Regrip before the next turn if needed.
